Welcome! This website is under construction. It shows a draft of the new **Typology of Methods Research (TYPE-ME)** - a living resource for methods researchers who work in the context of health research and psychology. The typology is based on an [ongoing consensus study](https://osf.io/4fxaz/overview).


::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Why do we need TYPE-ME?

Health research journals publish many types of methodological research, but definitions, boundaries, and terminology remain unclear.

This lack of clarity

* complicates planning and reporting,
* creates uncertainty about labels,
* limits searchability and indexing in research databases,
* reduces the visibility of methodological research as a field,
* obscures what constitutes methodological evidence, and
* hinders standard setting.

TYPE-ME brings these types together as one family and clarifies their similarities, differences, strengths, and difficult boundaries.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## What is methodological research?

Methodological research aims to develop, evaluate, refine, or provide guidance on research methods, support their implementation or de-implementation, or synthesize existing methodological research.

Methodological research addresses methods across the whole research lifecycle: planning, conducting, analyzing and interpreting, reporting, summarizing, evaluating, and implementing research.

Methodological research also addresses challenges that require methodological solutions and the consequences of methodological choices.

TYPE-ME focuses on research methods used in health research.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## How does TYPE-ME organize methodological research?

TYPE-ME organizes methodological research along two cross-cutting dimensions:

* **Approach:** How do researchers conduct the methodological research?
* **Purpose:** Why do researchers conduct the methodological research?

The detailed typology includes 15 approach types and 13 purpose types. One approach can serve several purposes, and one purpose can draw on several approaches.

For each type, we provide a definition, possible labels, strengths and limitations, examples, and boundary notes where needed.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## What can I use TYPE-ME for?

TYPE-ME can help with:

* planning, conducting, and reporting methodological research;
* classifying and indexing methodological research;
* designing projects that combine several types of methodological research;
* developing guidance for specific methodological research types;
* defining methodological evidence; and
* teaching methodological research.

Treat the types as archetypes, not as mutually exclusive boxes. A study may combine several approaches or fall between related types. Use the detailed typology as a conceptual core; for teaching, communication, or broad classification, [adapt the typology to your needs or use the condensed version](simplified.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## How did we develop TYPE-ME?

An international team of 11 methodologists developed TYPE-ME through repeated discussion, written feedback, and testing.

In two testing rounds, team members independently classified 52 methodological research articles from 26 journals. Testing helped us refine definitions and labels, clarify difficult boundaries, and document remaining disagreements.

We will continue to refine TYPE-ME through application, user feedback, and further testing.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## How can I cite the typology?

Please cite the typology as follows:

[Manuscript in preparation]

:::
